landing.title: Yawaragi
landing.intro: Explore Japanese sake through guided flavor profiles, label scans, and a chat that learns what you enjoy. Built for the curious — at any starting point.
landing.sectionScanBody: Point your camera at a bottle. We read the kanji and surface what's known about the brewery, the rice, and the style.
landing.sectionChatBody: Tell us what you usually drink. We translate it into Japanese brewer vocabulary and suggest sake that fits.
landing.sectionProfileBody: Over time, your reactions shape a personal flavor map you can compare with others.

hero.photoAlt: A chilled bottle of 木戸泉 (Kidoizumi) sake

landing.heading: Know what's in the cup.
landing.lead: Point your phone at a sake label. Yawaragi tells you what it is, how it tastes, and whether you'll like it. One tap and it's in your journal.
landing.smallPrint: Free · no account needed · for adults 18+
landing.featureIdentifyBody: Kanji or romaji — the camera reads whichever the bottle gives you. No camera? Use a photo or type the name.
landing.featureRateBody: The star is the save. Add a note if you want, or detailed tasting notes later.
landing.featurePalateBody: After three tastings it shows what you like — and why. Already know whisky or wine? Start from a drink you love.
landing.privacyBody: Everything works on your phone without an account. Nothing is posted publicly, and your ratings are only shared — anonymously — if you choose to.

ageGate.lead: Scan a label, keep a tasting journal, and watch your own palate take shape.
ageGate.lawLine: Under German youth-protection law (JMStV), Yawaragi is for adults 18 and over.

under18.title: Come back when you are 18
under18.body: Yawaragi is an information service about Japanese sake. German law requires us to limit alcohol-related content to adults. You are welcome to return once you are 18 or older.

comingSoon.title: Coming soon
comingSoon.body: Yawaragi is preparing its launch for German-speaking visitors. The English preview is available today; the German edition follows once the legal foundations (Impressum, privacy) are in place.

romajiDisclosure.title: Spelled by a machine
romajiDisclosure.body: Sakenowa publishes each sake's name in Japanese. The Latin spelling beside it was produced by an AI model reading the Japanese, so it is an approximation of how the name sounds — not a second official name. The Japanese is the one the brewery uses, and it is what we match on.

disclosure.title: About these flavor words

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.intro: Yawaragi is operated by the maintainer named in the Impressum, who acts as the data controller under GDPR Art. 4(7). This page lists the categories of personal data we process and the third-party processors we rely on. It is updated alongside every release that introduces or changes a processing operation, per ADR-0009.
privacy.anonymousSessionBody: When you use a feature that calls a paid AI service (today: the label scan), we set a signed, opaque cookie named `yawaragi_session` with a 24-hour sliding lifetime. The cookie holds a random identifier — never your name, email, or IP. We use it together with a short-lived hash of your IP address (kept only as a query key, never stored as plaintext and never written to a database or log) to cap how many scans a single visitor can run per day, so the AI bill stays bounded. Lawful basis: legitimate interest in cost protection of paid AI surfaces (GDPR Art. 6(1)(f)). Retention: 24 hours, sliding. Data residency: EU (rate-limit storage hosted in an EU region of Upstash Redis).
privacy.processorVercel: Vercel, Inc. (USA) — hosting, build, and edge logs. Transfer mechanism: EU-US Data Privacy Framework plus EU SCCs as a fallback. Vercel processes service-generated data (request logs, build metadata) as an independent controller.
privacy.processorSupabase: Supabase, Inc. — Postgres database for the Sakenowa reference mirror and (from Phase 2.5) user-scoped tables. Project region: eu-central-1 (Frankfurt). Transfer mechanism: EU SCCs (Modules 2 and 3) governed by Irish law. Service usage telemetry is processed by Supabase as an independent controller under Art. 6(1)(f) (billing, security, service improvement). Breach notification SLA: 48 hours.
privacy.processorUpstash: Upstash, Inc. — Redis key-value store hosted in an EU region (e.g. eu-central-1 Frankfurt) used as the rate-limit budget store for the anonymous-session cookie described above. Stored data: the salted SHA-256 hash of the visitor IP and the opaque session id, each with a 24-hour TTL. No plaintext IPs, no account identifiers. Transfer mechanism: EU SCCs (data does not leave the EU region). Data Processing Agreement: pending signature before Production deployment.
privacy.processorClerk: Clerk, Inc. (USA) — user authentication (sign-in, session, JWT issuance) starting Phase 2.5. Data categories: email address, given name, family name, and short-lived email-verification codes used to confirm sign-in. Lawful basis: Art. 6(1)(b) (performance of contract — Clerk holds the credentials required to operate an account). Transfer mechanism: EU-US Data Privacy Framework plus EU SCCs as a fallback. Retention: until account deletion or 24 months of account inactivity (per ADR-0009). Clerk does not publish a fixed breach-notification SLA; per the breach runbook, we treat an unconfirmed Clerk incident as starting an internal 24-hour clock toward BayLDA Art. 33 notification.
privacy.sakenowaNote: Sake brand and brewery reference data is mirrored from the public Sakenowa Data API (muro.sakenowa.com). The mirror itself contains no personal data.
privacy.retention: Cookies expire after one year. Phase 2 reference data is retained for the lifetime of the service. Future per-user data (Phase 2.5+) follows the retention rules in ADR-0009.
privacy.contact: For data-subject requests (access, rectification, erasure, portability), use the email address in the Impressum.

temperatureTerms.title: Serving temperatures
temperatureTerms.intro: Sake is served across a range of temperatures, and each step has a Japanese name. The degrees are approximate; what matters is how the same sake changes from one step to the next.

notes.yukibie: Snow-chilled: as cold as it gets. Aroma is muted and the finish turns sharp and clean.
notes.hanabie: Flower-chilled: cold from the fridge. Crisp, with the aroma still held back.
notes.suzuhie: Cool, just under room temperature. The aroma starts to open while it stays fresh.
notes.joon: Room temperature: the sake as it is, with nothing hidden or added.
notes.nurukan: Lukewarm, a little above body heat. Rounder and softer; umami comes forward.
notes.atsukan: Hot. Drier and sharper, best with fuller, savory sakes.
